properties.name: Four surface fixes from Alex's report: add_epoch names the sequence it needs, get_node resolves by id alone, Interface.auth says it is authentication, and a bulk write can be checked without being written
properties.rationale: Each is the fix the root-cause fact named, not the reporter's literal ask where those differed. (2) Alex offered auto-assign OR say-so-in-the-error; the record (chg:the-philosophy-epoch-makes-room-for-a-cut) shows sequences are spaced on purpose, so say-so shipped and auto-assign stays open on dec:idea-add-epoch-assigns-the-next-sequence-or-names-it. (3) The prefix is a convention not a rule, so a by-id read must be able to SEE a collision — node_type_index cannot (first type wins), hence the new resolver that scans every type and the refusal on >1. (4) `auth` is a mechanism because seam pairing keys on it (dec:pairing-role-placement); the real gap is the deferred personnel vocabulary, so the fix points at it rather than inventing a role field. PropertyDef carries no description, so the hint lives in the typed handler; the create_nodes/schema-validation path still only lists legal values — a bound. (5) Alex's 'resend the whole payload' is FORCED by atomicity (my first brainstorm draft said otherwise and was corrected); check_only removes the iterate-by-rejection cost without touching dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings — a requested check returning applied:false is not a rejected write dressed as success, which is what that decision forbids. WHAT WAS NOT DONE: the same check_only on record_asked_questions (a prompt generator, not a user-facing bulk write) and release_includes_all (already has apply:true as its dry-run). Built on Anthony's ruling of 2026-09-05: 'I want to do all five fixes.'
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Alex (v0.47.0, 2026-09-05), items 2-5; item 1 is chg:currency-has-a-non-linux-answer. (2) add_epoch: when `sequence` is omitted on CREATE, the handler pre-checks before the generic required-field helper and refuses naming the current maximum ('highest existing sequence is N across K epochs, N+1 is next, leaving a gap keeps room'), or 'no epochs yet'. NOT auto-assigned — a sequence is a position claim and sequences are deliberately spaced. Also lists any other missing fields so it stays all-at-once. (3) get_node takes GetNodeReq: `node_type` optional; when omitted the id is resolved via the new core `node_types_holding(id)` (a sorted scan of every type); zero holders -> {node: null}; one -> that type; MORE THAN ONE -> REFUSED naming them, never guessed. delete_node keeps the strict TypedIdReq on purpose. 17 test call sites migrated. (4) set_interface_spec pre-checks `auth` against the schema's enum and refuses with: AUTHENTICATION mechanism, read by seam pairing, legal values listed, and 'if you meant AUTHORIZATION there is no field yet (req:vocabulary-covers-personnel, deferred) — Actor INTERACTS_WITH + describe the role'. The Req doc-comment and schema/structure.yaml description say the same, so the tool schema teaches before the refusal does. (5) `check_only: true` on create_nodes, create_edges, set_artifact_checksums, acknowledge_gaps: core bulk::atomic gains a check_only mode (validate every item, ALWAYS discard), BulkReport carries `check_only`, five `*_with(check_only)` core siblings (originals delegate), and bulk_result returns a CHECK payload {check_only, applied:false, checked, would_apply, failures, note}. The all-or-nothing refusal now says plainly that the valid items were discarded too and the WHOLE batch must be resent, and offers check_only. Pins in tools.rs (four tests), observed failing first (E0422/E0425 — the types and fns did not exist). core 1578/0, mcp 356/0, fmt/clippy clean, validate_schema OK, toolsnaps regenerated (6 changed).
